corrections.text: The article says the quote from Google that The Hacker News reports ("a significant rise in automated submissions, the vast majority of which are not valid") "may come from the notice or a follow-up post". The editor read the notice as it appears in Google's public GitHub copy of the OSS VRP rules (google/bughunters, commit f8bf23a, September 30): it announces that Google is no longer accepting product vulnerabilities from October 1, 2026 and commits to a Q1 2027 update, and it gives no reason and does not contain the quote. The October 1 X post does not contain it either, so the wording "automated" rests on The Hacker News's report alone.

The Implications section says "GitHub gives newcomers up to four initial submissions". GitHub's July 22 post says "HackerOne's platform gives researchers who don't meet the threshold up to four initial submissions".

The Implications section places Google's move from a proof requirement at "March 20". That is the date of InfoWorld's report; the cited sources do not give the date of Google's own announcement, and The Hacker News says only that Google began requiring stronger proof for some tiers in March 2026.
